traps: Ticker collision: BSE symbol CHTR (Chatterbox Technologies Ltd, an Indian BSE SME influencer-marketing agency, market cap ~Rs 54 Cr) is identical to the US ticker CHTR = Charter Communications, Inc. (a ~$70B US cable company). This is the manifest's headline hostile trait for this slot -- an automated pipeline keying purely off the bare symbol 'CHTR' with no exchange/region qualifier risks silently merging or substituting Charter Communications' US financials for this Indian SME's, or vice versa.

Pre-IPO EPS is not comparable to post-IPO EPS: standalone annual EPS jumps from Rs 663.30 (FY Mar2024) to Rs 8.51 (FY Mar2025) to Rs 6.50 (FY Mar2026) purely because Equity Capital jumped from Rs 0.13 Cr to Rs 10.42 Cr to Rs 14.14 Cr across those same years (SME IPO + a follow-on raise), i.e. the share count multiplied roughly 100x. Any YoY EPS growth calculation that spans the IPO year will show a nonsensical -98%-type 'decline' that is purely a share-count/dilution artifact, not an earnings collapse -- a naive pipeline computing EPS CAGR across this boundary would badly mislead.

SME issuers file HALF-YEARLY, not quarterly, financial results (see latest_results) -- a pipeline that expects a quarterly cadence (as it would for a mainboard stock) will either show stale/blank 'quarter' data or wrongly label a half-year figure as a quarter.

Public brand names (Chtrbox, Chtrsocial) used in marketing/media coverage match neither the legal name (Chatterbox Technologies Limited) nor the ticker's plain-English reading -- a name-based resolver searching only for 'Chtrbox' or 'Chtrsocial' may fail to resolve to this scrip at all.

BSE 'Sector' (Consumer Discretionary) and BSE 'IndustryNew' (Media, Entertainment & Publication) fields disagree with each other and with screener.in's own sector labelling in ways that could cause inconsistent sector-based screens/comparisons depending which BSE field a pipeline reads.
